# Sources this skill cites

Each entry gives the exact quote relied on and the date it was checked. When you cite a rule to the user, name it in prose from the **Source** line (for example "SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2") and put the id after it, so the text reads for people. ## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-fully-secured

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.3: fully secured, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A 7(a) loan is fully secured when liens on the business’s fixed assets (real estate, machinery and equipment), at adjusted values, reach the loan amount.
- **Quote:** "SBA considers a loan as “fully secured” if the Lender has taken security interests in all available fixed assets of the Applicant with a combined Net Book Value as adjusted below, up to the loan amount. For 7(a) loans, the term “fixed assets” means real estate, including land and structures, machinery and equipment owned by the business or an EPC."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-insurance-credit-memo

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: insurance in the credit memo, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The lender's credit memo for an acquisition addresses life insurance (on whom and how much, or why none) and business hazard and liability insurance.
- **Quote:** "Insurance Requirements, including: Life Insurance – on whom and how much. If life insurance is not required, provide justification. Business hazard and liability insurances."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-lien-limit

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.3: lien amount limits, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A lien on personal real estate may be limited to the collateral shortfall or to 150% of the equity.
- **Quote:** "Liens on personal real estate may be limited to the amount of the collateral shortfall. In addition, liens on personal real estate may be limited to 150% of the equity in the collateral."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-other-guarantors

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A: other guarantors, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The lender may require guaranties from others regardless of ownership percentage.
- **Quote:** "When deemed necessary for credit or other reasons, SBA or, for a loan processed on a delegated basis, the SBA Lender, may require other appropriate individuals or entities to provide full or limited guaranties of the loan without regard to the percentage of their ownership interests, if any."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-owner-financial-statement

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 20: owner financial statements, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Owners of 20% or more and proposed guarantors give a personal financial statement (SBA Form 413 or equivalent) dated within 90 days; business financial statements must be within 120 days.
- **Quote:** "Owner Financial Statement for all owners of 20% or more (including the assets of the owner’s spouse and minor children), and proposed guarantors, except Supplemental Guarantors, Lenders may use SBA Form 413 or their own equivalent form signed and dated within 90 days of submission to SBA. Business financial statements must be dated within 120 days of submission to SBA."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-partial-change-guaranty

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: selling owner who keeps under 20%, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In a partial change of ownership, a selling owner who keeps less than 20% must guarantee the full loan for at least two years after final disbursement.
- **Quote:** "Any selling owner (one who receives loan proceeds in exchange for selling part of their ownership) who remains as a direct or indirect owner and owns less than 20% of the business post-sale must provide a full guaranty for the full loan amount pursuant to 13 CFR 120.160(a). The term of the guaranty must be for at least two years after final loan disbursement."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-personal-guaranty

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A: personal guaranties, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Every individual owning 20% or more of the borrower must give an unlimited full personal guaranty.
- **Quote:** "Any individual who has direct and/or indirect ownership of 20% or more of an Applicant must provide an unlimited full guaranty."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-personal-real-estate

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.3: collateral shortfall and personal real estate, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** If business assets do not fully secure the loan, the lender must take available equity in personal real estate owned by 20% owners and guarantors.
- **Quote:** "Must take available equity in the personal real estate (residential and investment property including other commercial real estate regardless of whether the owner is actively running a business at the investment property) that is solely owned by any Co-Borrowers, direct and/or indirect owners of 20% or more of the Applicant and guarantors except Supplemental Guarantors."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-real-estate-equity-threshold

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.3: 25% equity threshold, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Real estate with less than 25% equity need not be taken as collateral to meet the fully secured test.
- **Quote:** "SBA does not require a Lender to collateralize a loan with real estate (including commercial, residential and investment properties owned by the Applicant or personally by the owners) to meet the “fully secured” definition when the equity in the real estate is less than 25% of the property’s fair market value."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-spouse-guaranty

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A: guaranty of spouse, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A spouse owning under 20% must guarantee in full when spouses and minor children together own 20% or more.
- **Quote:** "Each spouse owning less than 20% of an Applicant must personally guarantee the loan in full when the combined ownership interest of both spouses and minor children is 20% or more."
